coordinate_frame: Workstation metres, +X east, +Y north, +Z up; radians; wxyz quaternions
objective: Complete the declared assembly/transport task correctly and efficiently; allocation, local motion and collaboration are Agent choices.
rules: Move all 2 numbered payload assemblies from their individual initial positions toward the common GOAL. START marks the route origin; returning scattered payloads to START is not required.
Route regions and arrows indicate progress. Grasp points, handover locations, robot teams, allocation and execution order are planner choices. Independent work may run concurrently.

Airborne transport requires at least two actual beam grasps. Establish receiving support before releasing a sender. Every assembly must undergo a real qualified airborne handover; the receiving team may retain an existing holder.
Grasp the red timber, not a pendant, ring or shaft. Keep the whole assembly clear of table and floor during airborne transport, except for the allowed final GOAL landing.
Any final placement in GOAL is allowed, including cargo contact and stacking. Oracle packing centers and contact-free separation are not task requirements.

Each timber must have at least 70 percent of its centreline length in the vertical space above the GOAL outline. Final completion requires release from every robot; direct or indirect table support is not required.

Drops and violations remain recorded. Only the last established sending team may recover a dropped assembly; a receiver cannot pick it up to bypass an airborne handover. No reset, respawn or history erasure.
Only ordinary robot actuators and real contacts may change the live task. No hand welds, object-state writes, hidden-state tools, runtime physics changes or stabilizing attachments.

A handover qualifies only while the timber is off the table and at least two current holders keep it: a new arm must hold the timber for at least 0.2 seconds before a current holder lets go. A timber placed in GOAL without a qualified handover is not complete. Pushing or dragging a timber along the table never counts as transport.
Collisions, drops and other process events are recorded separately. Recover using ordinary robot actions; do not reset, respawn or erase history.

completion.scope: Every timber has had a qualified airborne handover, is at least 70% above painted GOAL and is released; other process events are reported separately.

mechanism.initial_distribution: Separate positions along the route; each travels rightward to the common destination

# Relay

## Shared payloads

Plan the relative motion of all supporting tools as well as their individual
paths. A same-cycle start does not guarantee matched arrival or prevent internal
loads. Choose support contacts and bearing direction for load moments, not jaw
aperture alone; if a lift changes the payload pose unexpectedly, reassess that
geometry before repeating the motion. Treat support and manipulation as coupled
work: control coupled robots directly together, or give them to one bounded
delegate, rather than splitting coupled support across independent scopes.

## Handovers

Choose teams, the route and handover points from reach, observations and the
cost of each regrasp. Preserve receiver access and sender withdrawal when choosing
a grasp. Before releasing an existing hold, establish the receiver's support from
allowed RGB and robot evidence; width-based grasp feedback alone is insufficient.
Update the shared reference after slip or reorientation.

Every timber needs a qualified airborne handover before it can count as complete, so
plan one for each timber even when a single team could reach GOAL. Keep at least two
current holders on the timber while the new arm takes hold, and hold that overlap for
at least 0.2 seconds before a current holder lets go. Dragging or pushing a timber
along the table does not count, and neither does a handover made after a drop until
the last sending team has recovered the timber.

## At the goal

Check each assembly separately against the completion rule from permitted views,
and confirm that every robot has released it and the jaws have cleared it before
proposing completion. After a drop or collision, reason from the actual scene and
recover with ordinary actions.
